title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 524-526 of Grothendieck's numbering). SL2(Z) is the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, generated by sigma (order 4) and rho (order 6). Grothendieck works with group schemes over a base S, in particular the 'absolute modular case' S = Spec Z:
- T_rho and T_sigma are the centralizer 'tori' of rho and sigma in GL2. Over Z these are Res_{Z[zeta_6]/Z} G_m and Res_{Z[i]/Z} G_m. They are not tori at the ramified primes 3 and 2.
- ST and S'T are the subgroups with det = 1 and det = ±1 respectively.
- N'_sigma is the normalizer of T_sigma.
- M_{rho,sigma} is a group scheme with M = R_{rho,sigma}·SG and Ker(Theta~) = R_{rho,sigma}.
- M°_{rho,sigma} is its neutral (index-type) piece, whose centre is R° = ST_rho × ST_sigma × G_m by (75), p. 514.

Previous page. The centre maps to the centre of PG, which is trivial, so Cent(M) ⊂ R. Since R commutes with SG, Cent(M) = Cent(R) = S'T_rho × Cent(SN'_sigma) × G_m. The group mu2 = SN'_sigma/ST_sigma acts faithfully on ST_sigma by inversion. Hence Cent(SN'_sigma) = (ST_sigma)^{mu2} = 2-torsion of ST_sigma, which equals mu2 when 2 is invertible on S.

This page.
1. A boxed cross-reference to a diagram. It records mu2 ⊂ SN'_sigma, identified with the subgroup ST_sigma ∩ G_m.
2. The conclusion, explicitly hedged 'je crois': (128) Cent(M_{rho,sigma}) ≅ S'T_rho × mu2 × G_m ⊂ R ≅ S'T_rho × SN'_sigma × G_m.
3. Intersecting with M° gives (129) Cent(M) ∩ M° = ST_rho × mu2 × G_m ⊂ R° ≅ ST_rho × ST_sigma × G_m.
4. Integer points in the absolute modular case:
   - T_rho(Z) = Z[zeta_6]^* ≅ Z/6.
   - T_sigma(Z) = Z[i]^* ≅ Z/4.
   - G_m(Z) = mu2(Z) = ±1.
   Hence (131) Cent(M)(Z) ≅ Z/6 × {±1} × {±1}, of order 24, and (132) Cent(M°)(Z) = R°(Z) ≅ Z/6 × Z/4 × {±1}, of order 48.
5. Summary diagram (133), a commutative square of strict inclusions of group schemes, with relative dimensions:
   - Top row (dim 3): R° → R, with quotient mu2 × mu2, coming from S'T_rho/ST_rho and SN'_sigma/ST_sigma.
   - Bottom row (dim 2): Cent(M) ∩ M° → Cent(M), with quotient mu2.
   - Vertical arrows: inclusions of centres.

The next page interprets the integer points of the two right-hand/left-hand groups as Aut(M)(Z). It introduces Sigma = {±1}^3 and a canonical homomorphism from a group attached to M_{0,3} into M_{rho,sigma}(Z^)/Sigma. So this page is bookkeeping of automorphism/centre groups needed to make that arithmetic (Galois/GT-type) map well defined modulo the right finite group.
errors: (128)/(131) assert Cent(SN'_sigma) = mu2 over an arbitrary base. The struck-out computation on the previous page shows this is proved only when 2 is invertible. Over Z, T_sigma = Res_{Z[i]/Z} G_m is not a torus at 2, since Z[i] is ramified there. The 2-torsion of ST_sigma (equations 2vc^2 = 0, 2cd = 0, d^2 - vc^2 = 1) is then a priori larger than mu2 in characteristic 2, possibly non-flat. Grothendieck flags this himself with 'je crois'.

In (130) the underbrace under SN'_sigma(Z) reads T_sigma(Z) = Z/4Z. But SN'_sigma(Z) itself is an extension of mu2 by mu4 (order 8, non-abelian), not Z/4. The annotation must refer to the torus part only. Similarly the brace under G_m(Z) records mu2(Z) = G_m(Z) = ±1.
The horizontal arrows in (133) are inclusions; the label 'quotient mu2×mu2' / 'quotient mu2' means the cokernel. For the bottom row the quotient is S'T_rho/ST_rho ≅ mu2, consistent with the formulas.

ideas.what: Computation of the centre of a group scheme M_{rho,sigma} built from the centralizer tori of the order-6 and order-4 generators of SL2(Z), over a general base and over Z.
ideas.modern_name: Centres of group schemes; centralizers of elliptic elements; Weil restrictions Res_{O_K/Z} G_m (non-reductive at ramified primes).

ideas.what: Integer points: Z[zeta_6]^* = Z/6, Z[i]^* = Z/4, giving automorphism/centre groups of orders 24 and 48 with index-2 relations.
ideas.modern_name: Units of quadratic orders; stabilizers of elliptic points j = 0, 1728.

ideas.what: Square (133) of inclusions of centres relating M°, M and their centres, as preparation for a canonical map from an M_{0,3}-related (Galois/GT-type) group to M_{rho,sigma}(Z^)/Sigma.
ideas.modern_name: Scheme-theoretic model of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 and Galois/GT actions on the profinite completion.
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara; Grothendieck's Longue Marche (1981, partially published)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related themes in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois; exact construction unsure

missed.claim: The centre of M_{rho,sigma} over Z (2 not invertible) is left undetermined: only mu2 ⊂ Cent(SN'_sigma) is proved, with equality on fibres where 2 is invertible. Behaviour at 2 (and the analogous ramification at 3 for T_rho) is not resolved.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It would matter only if one wants an integral (Spec Z) version of Grothendieck's group-scheme model of the modular group. The computation is routine for a specialist.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of centres and their integer points within a larger unpublished construction. The construction itself (M_{rho,sigma}, the map in (136) on the next page) may be of interest, but nothing on this page is a new result.
transcription_corrections: (128) should read Cent with double underline, '≃ S'T_ρ × μ_2 × G_m ⊂ R_{ρ,σ} ≃ S'T_ρ × SN'_σ × G_m', as transcribed. The box above contains '(131) μ_2' ⊂ SN'_σ' and below it '‖ (ST_σ ∩? μ_2)' with an erased word, plus 'sous-groupe de ...' and 'Diagramme p. ...'.
Bottom-right of (133): the image shows 'S'T_ρ × μ_2 × G_m', overwritten from 'SN'_σ'. It is not 'μ_2^Σ'.
(131) label is written '(131)' (second use of the number), and (132) is '(132)'. The transcription is fine, but note the numbering 128-131 is reused from the previous page.
